title: The Power of Advertising
text:
Advertising is everywhere in modern life, from billboards on busy streets to short videos on mobile phones. Companies use these messages to persuade people to buy products, and they often repeat the same slogan many times. Many advertisements rely on emotion rather than facts, showing happy families or famous people to make a product seem more desirable.

However, critics argue that some advertisements can mislead consumers, especially when they hide important information in small print. Governments in many countries therefore set rules about honest claims. Thoughtful viewers learn to question what they see and compare products before they decide to spend money.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, where can advertising be found?
According to the second paragraph, what can some advertisements hide?
What can be inferred about advertisements that rely on emotion rather than facts?
options: They may persuade people without providing much evidence
They are banned in most countries

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about thoughtful viewers?
options: They are less likely to be misled by advertising
They trust every slogan they see

vocabulary.definition: to make someone do or believe something by giving reasons
a short, memorable phrase used in advertising
to make someone believe something that is not true
people who buy and use products or services

paragraph_translations: Reklamcılık, kalabalık caddelerdeki afişlerden cep telefonlarındaki kısa videolara kadar modern hayatın her yerinde. Şirketler bu mesajları insanları ürün satın almaya ikna etmek için kullanır ve genellikle aynı sloganı defalarca tekrarlar. Birçok reklam gerçeklere değil duygulara dayanır; mutlu aileleri veya ünlü kişileri göstererek ürünü daha çekici göstermeye çalışır.

Ancak eleştirmenler, bazı reklamların özellikle önemli bilgileri küçük puntolarla gizlediğinde tüketicileri yanıltabileceğini savunuyor. Birçok ülkedeki hükümetler bu nedenle dürüst iddialarla ilgili kurallar koyar. Bilinçli izleyiciler ise karar vermeden önce gördüklerini sorgulamayı ve ürünleri karşılaştırmayı öğrenir.
